notes.text: Preserved as a separate open item when closing the agreed S0–S5 technical deliverable. S4u per-user mutation fairness and export quota recovery were delivered in PR #73; this item is specifically the remaining global manual backup idempotency-history limit, not those completed user-export changes.

problem: Manual backup idempotency records are retained up to 1024 keys. At the bound, new manual admission is refused; no supported reset or rollover protocol exists. Offline backup create uses the same BackupOperations path and does not bypass this bound.

risk.rollback: Retain immutable receipts and fail closed at the bound until a verified replacement protocol exists.

scope: Design an explicit bounded history/recovery protocol before implementing any key retirement, preserving existing retry outcomes across restart, restore and concurrent admission.
Keep retained keys and safe refusal until that protocol is reviewed. Never recommend deleting or hand-editing the ledger or blind TTL/latest-N pruning.
Account for shared ledger/catalog/disk limits and the independent scheduled-service history budget; avoid weakening protected backups or introducing another executor.
source: Retained operational follow-up from PR #72 / n8n execution 9579, originally tracked in RWK-20260928-sqlite-data-safety.
title: Define safe operator recovery at the manual backup history limit
validation: Exhaust the manual-key budget and prove existing retries still replay safely while fresh admission refuses.

For any future rollover implementation, verify duplicate/conflicting keys, in-flight operations, restart, restore rollback and uncertain publication without repeated side effects or lost protected material.
Document an operator procedure and its limits; a host/key/rollout decision alone does not resolve the capacity protocol.
value: Keep long-running operator backup use available without replaying forgotten requests or deleting recovery evidence.
